claims.title: Detect updates that match no photo row
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Detect updates that match no photo row**

This only treats a database error as failure. An `UPDATE ... WHERE id = photoId` that matches zero rows can complete without an error, so a deleted/stale `photoId` will upload the processed asset but leave no `processed_url` update while this function resolves successfully. The pipeline will report success and leave an orphaned upload, which makes this failure difficult to diagnose.

Request the updated row (or an affected-row count) and throw when none was updated. For example, append `.select('id').single()` to the update and handle its error, or otherwise explicitly validate that exactly one row matched.

claims.title: Per-photo outputs share one storage object
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Per-photo outputs share one storage object**

Required: `storagePath` is derived only from `listingId`, while this function is invoked for a specific `intakePhotoId`. If a skipped-background or jewelry listing has multiple photos, every invocation uploads to `intake/<listingId>/processed.png`; later uploads replace the object that earlier photo rows reference. The earlier photos will consequently display the last processed image. Include `intakePhotoId` (or another per-photo identifier) in the storage path before calling either processing path.

claims.title: The historical behavior is described incorrectly
Honor EXIF orientation before producing the JPEG
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Honor EXIF orientation before producing the JPEG**

The new raw-photo path sends original camera uploads directly through this helper. `sharp(...).jpeg().toBuffer()` does not preserve the input EXIF metadata, and without an explicit auto-orientation operation the encoded pixel data remains in its stored sensor orientation. Consequently, portrait photos from devices that rely on EXIF orientation will display sideways/upside-down once `processed_url` is preferred. Apply Sharp's auto-orientation (for example, `.rotate()`) before trimming/filtering, and add an EXIF-oriented fixture to cover this path.

claims.title: Skip-bg toggle can continue displaying an existing background-removed image
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Skip-bg toggle can continue displaying an existing background-removed image**

When a listing already has `processed_url` values from the background-removal path and the user subsequently enables “BG removal off,” this now still selects those existing processed images. Previously `skipBgRemoval` forced `raw_url`, so the toggle immediately honored the user's request. Keep the skip-aware fallback for already-processed listings, or ensure the toggle clears/replaces every existing `processed_url` before this component renders.

claims.title: Remove review-history attribution from source comment
claims.text:
🟢 **Low**

**Remove review-history attribution from source comment**

The implementation rationale is useful, but embedding `codexreviewbot, PR #56` and a cross-file historical comparison makes this production comment depend on temporary review context and likely to rot. Keep the durable collision rationale without the review provenance.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
  // Key outputs by intakePhotoId so each photo in a listing has a distinct storage object.
```

claims.title: Skip toggle can retain a background-removed image
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Skip toggle can retain a background-removed image**

This removes the prior skip-mode fallback to `raw_url`. A listing that was processed normally (so `processed_url` contains the background-removed image) and is subsequently switched to “BG removal off” will continue to display that old processed image rather than the raw image. The new raw-processing path only helps if it has already replaced `processed_url`; this UI change provides no distinction between a crop/denoise-only output and a prior background-removed output. Clear/regenerate `processed_url` when enabling skip mode, or persist output provenance and select the appropriate variant.

claims.title: Reprocess every intake photo when toggling the setting
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Reprocess every intake photo when toggling the setting**

`runStep4bPhotoRoom` explicitly supports multiple intake photos per listing (and keys each output by `intakePhotoId`), but this query selects a single intake photo. Consequently, toggling skip on/off for a listing with multiple intake photos only refreshes at most one variant before the flag is saved; the remaining photos retain processed URLs from the prior mode and are still preferred by the UI. Fetch all matching intake photos and reprocess each (or reject the toggle if the full set cannot be reprocessed) before persisting the flag.

claims.title: Photo lookup failures are silently treated as no photo to reprocess
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Photo lookup failures are silently treated as no photo to reprocess**

`maybeSingle()` is used for a collection that the new step4b path explicitly supports having multiple intake photos for, and its error is discarded. If there are multiple intake rows, or this query otherwise fails, `photo` is null/undefined; the handler then skips reprocessing and still persists the flag change with a 200 response. Users will be told the preference changed while the existing `processed_url` images retain the prior variant.

**Hidden errors:** a multiple-row result and any Supabase read error are both converted into the same silent no-op.

**Recommendation:** capture and handle the query error before changing the listing flag. Query all intake photos rather than `maybeSingle()`, and reprocess every eligible photo (or reject the toggle with a clear error if the application only supports one). This keeps the preference and every displayed processed image consistent.

claims.title: Turning skip off applies background removal to jewelry despite the pipeline rule
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Turning skip off applies background removal to jewelry despite the pipeline rule**

The normal step4b path unconditionally routes `jewelry` through `processRawPhoto`, regardless of `skip_background_removal`, because removal is known to damage that category. This toggle route does not load or evaluate the category, so a jewelry listing that has skip enabled can be toggled off and immediately be reprocessed with `removeBackground`. The same listing would go back to the raw-processing path on a subsequent intake pipeline run, yielding inconsistent output for identical listing state.

**User impact:** jewelry photos can unexpectedly receive the very background-removal treatment the category safeguard was added to avoid.

**Recommendation:** centralize the background-removal eligibility decision used by step4b and this route, and load the category needed to apply it before choosing `removeBg` during reprocessing.

claims.title: Honor the jewelry background-removal exclusion during toggles
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Honor the jewelry background-removal exclusion during toggles**

`runStep4bPhotoRoom` treats jewelry as an unconditional background-removal exclusion, independently of `skip_background_removal`. This route does not load or check the category, so switching a jewelry listing from `skip=true` to `skip=false` calls `removeBackground` and overwrites `processed_url` with a background-removed variant. Because consumers now always prefer `processed_url`, that output is displayed despite the category policy. Preserve the crop-only path for jewelry here as well, or prevent this toggle from changing the hard-coded category behavior.

claims.title: Legacy skipped photos are never reprocessed when the setting changes
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Legacy skipped photos are never reprocessed when the setting changes**

**Confidence: 96/100.** This guard treats a missing `processed_url` as an in-progress pipeline, but the PR description establishes that completed skip-background listings previously also have no `processed_url`. If one of those existing listings turns skip off, this route skips `removeBg`, updates the flag to false, and leaves the unprocessed raw photo in place; the route comment also states that no later intake step will be triggered. Distinguish an actively running intake pipeline explicitly, or reprocess whenever an intake photo has `raw_url` so legacy skipped listings receive the variant matching the new setting.

claims.title: Reprocess photos even when no prior variant exists
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Reprocess photos even when no prior variant exists**

The `processed_url` guard leaves previously skipped listings permanently unprocessed when a user turns skip off. Before this PR, skip-background intake photos intentionally had `processed_url = null`; for such a listing, this toggle updates `skip_background_removal` to `false` but never calls `removeBg`, so the UI continues falling back to the raw image despite background removal now being enabled. The new test labels this state as “mid-pipeline,” but it is also the normal persisted state for existing skipped listings.

Use `raw_url` as the eligibility condition and coordinate with any in-flight intake processing as needed, rather than treating a missing derived URL as a reason to skip the requested reprocessing.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
    if (photo?.raw_url) {
```

claims.title: Handle every intake photo when toggling the setting
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Handle every intake photo when toggling the setting**

This is a single-row lookup, but the pipeline explicitly supports distinct intake-photo IDs and storage paths for more than one photo in a listing. Consequently a skip toggle cannot reprocess every intake image: a multi-photo result is not iterable here and is handled as a lookup failure (or, at best, only one image could be acted on). Users can therefore end up with a listing setting that no longer matches some displayed/analysis variants.

Select the intake-photo collection and reprocess each row with a `raw_url`; preserve the current fail-before-flag-update behavior if any individual processing operation fails. Add a route test with two intake photos that asserts both receive the appropriate processor.

claims.title: Reprocess all intake photos when the flag changes
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Reprocess all intake photos when the flag changes**

A listing can have multiple intake photos (the pipeline itself scopes output paths by `intakePhotoId`), but this query is constrained to one row. With two intake rows, `maybeSingle()` returns a lookup error and the toggle responds 500; even if it did return one, the other processed variant would remain stale. Fetch all intake photos and run the selected processing path for each before persisting the flag. Add a multiple-intake-photo toggle test.

claims.title: Existing skipped listings cannot be reprocessed after a toggle
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Existing skipped listings cannot be reprocessed after a toggle**

Required: The new raw-processing path exists specifically because skipped listings previously had no `processed_url`, but this guard excludes exactly those pre-existing rows. For an existing listing with `skip_background_removal = true`, `raw_url` present, and `processed_url = null`, toggling skip off updates the flag without calling `removeBg`; no later intake step remains to generate the requested background-removed output, so consumers continue to fall back to the raw image. Handle completed legacy rows with a null `processed_url` while still avoiding duplicate work for genuinely in-flight pipeline rows.

claims.title: Toggle reprocessing races with the intake worker
claims.text: Toggle reprocessing races with the intake worker

claims.title: Reprocess every intake photo on a toggle
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Reprocess every intake photo on a toggle**

**Confidence: 97%** — This uses a single-row lookup even though the pipeline explicitly supports distinct intake-photo IDs within one listing. On a listing with multiple `type = 'intake'` rows, this toggle cannot regenerate every processed variant, leaving some photos on the pre-toggle background-removal mode (and potentially preventing the toggle entirely if the single-row query rejects multiple results). Fetch all intake photos and reprocess each applicable row before committing the flag change, or enqueue a batch reprocessing job that does so.

claims.title: Do not skip reprocessing while the intake pipeline is in flight
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Do not skip reprocessing while the intake pipeline is in flight**

**Confidence: 91%** — A missing `processed_url` is treated as proof that the in-flight intake pipeline will honor the new flag. However, `runStep4bPhotoRoom` reads `skip_background_removal` before it calls its selected processor. If it reads `false`, then this request changes the flag to `true` while `processed_url` is still null, the already-running step can finish `removeBackground` afterward and write a background-removed image for a skip-enabled listing. The reverse transition has the same problem. Serialize/version the processing decision with the toggle, or arrange a reprocess after the in-flight step completes, rather than relying on `processed_url` being non-null.

claims.title: Toggle path still processes only one intake photo
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Toggle path still processes only one intake photo**

`runStep4bPhotoRoom` and its new test explicitly support multiple photos per listing, but this toggle flow fetches the entire listing's intake set through `maybeSingle()` and invokes a processor for only one result. Thus a listing with multiple intake photos cannot have all variants synchronized when the setting changes (and a multi-row result is treated as a lookup failure by this single-row flow). Fetch the intake-photo list and reprocess each photo with its own `processed-${photo.id}` path before persisting the flag. Otherwise users can toggle the setting successfully only for a subset of the listing's photos, leaving the rest stale.

claims.title: A completed legacy skipped photo is silently left unprocessed
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**A completed legacy skipped photo is silently left unprocessed**

The PR describes the pre-existing skip path as leaving `processed_url` unset. For exactly that persisted state, turning skip off sets `turningSkipOff`, but this guard prevents `removeBg` because `processed_url` is null; the handler then updates `skip_background_removal` and returns `{ ok: true }`. The user has requested background removal, receives success, and continues to see the raw image. The test labels this state as “still mid-pipeline,” but the selected columns cannot distinguish an in-flight new listing from a completed legacy skipped listing. Reprocess any toggled photo with a `raw_url`, or use an explicit pipeline/status signal to defer only genuinely in-flight photos and ensure completed rows are subsequently processed.

claims.title: Skip toggle handles only one intake photo
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Skip toggle handles only one intake photo**

**Test coverage criticality: 8/10.** Listings can contain multiple photos (the step4b tests explicitly exercise distinct photo IDs under one listing), but this query materializes a single `photo` and the subsequent reprocessing block can invoke a processor only once. Consequently, toggling the setting leaves other intake photos on the old variant (and a multi-row `maybeSingle()` result may prevent the toggle from completing at all). Select all matching intake photos and reprocess each before persisting the flag. Add a handler test with two intake rows that asserts both IDs are processed using the selected path.

claims.title: A failed flag update leaves the processed variant inconsistent with the saved setting
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**A failed flag update leaves the processed variant inconsistent with the saved setting**

The selected processor updates `photos.processed_url` before this final listing update. If this update fails, the handler returns 500 but leaves the new variant committed under the old flag. For example, turning skip on can replace a background-removed image with the raw crop/denoise variant while `skip_background_removal` remains false; consumers now always prefer `processed_url`, so they display an image that contradicts the persisted setting. Model the toggle and variant switch as a recoverable transition (for example, stage the output and atomically commit the listing/photo database state, with cleanup or retry handling) rather than committing the photo change before a separately fallible flag write.

claims.title: Reprocess all intake photos when toggling
claims.text:
🔴 **High**

**Reprocess all intake photos when toggling**

This query only permits a single intake row, but this PR explicitly supports distinct processed objects for multiple photos in one listing. Consequently, toggling either direction on a listing with multiple `type = 'intake'` photos will either produce a lookup error and return 500 or, at best, process only one photo; the remaining `processed_url` values retain the old variant despite the new setting.

Use a multi-row select and process every row with a `raw_url` before committing the flag. Keep the existing lookup-error handling, but iterate over the returned photos (and obtain API keys once for the background-removal branch). Add a route test with two intake photos that verifies both receive the corresponding processing path.

claims.title: Avoid persisting a new image variant when the flag update fails
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Avoid persisting a new image variant when the flag update fails**

Confidence: 88/100. `processRawPhoto`/`removeBackground` uploads and updates `photos.processed_url` before this listings update is attempted. If this update fails, the endpoint returns 500 and `skip_background_removal` retains its old value, but consumers now preferentially display the newly written, opposite variant. Make the toggle and processed-URL transition recoverable as one workflow—for example, retain the prior URL and compensate on a listings update failure, or persist a reprocessing state and finalize both updates atomically in a database transaction after the upload succeeds.

claims.title: Do not leave processed URLs changed after a failed flag update
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Do not leave processed URLs changed after a failed flag update**

By this point `processRaw`/`removeBg` has already uploaded a replacement and updated `photos.processed_url`. If the subsequent `listings` update fails (for example, a database/network failure), this returns an error but leaves the new processed variant persisted while `skip_background_removal` retains its old value. Since the UI now always prefers `processed_url`, users can see the newly requested variant even though the API told them the toggle failed. This failure path is also not logged, unlike the newly added lookup and processing failure paths.

Avoid independently committing these two pieces of state: have processing produce immutable/new object URLs without updating rows, then use a database transaction/RPC to atomically update the listing flag and all affected photo URLs. On a transaction failure, log the listing ID and operation and delete the newly uploaded objects. Add a test where the final listing update fails and assert that no photo URL visible to consumers has changed.

claims.title: A failed flag update leaves the processed image in the wrong mode
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**A failed flag update leaves the processed image in the wrong mode**

Criticality: 7/10. Reprocessing writes `photos.processed_url` (and overwrites the stable storage object) before this listing update. If this update fails, the endpoint returns 500 and retains the old `skip_background_removal` value, but the image has already been changed to the newly requested variant. Consumers now always prefer `processed_url`, so the displayed image no longer reflects the persisted setting. Make this transition recoverable/atomic (for example, preserve and restore the prior variant on a failed setting write, or model a pending transition), and add a test where photo processing succeeds but the final listings update fails.

claims.title: Avoid committing a photo variant before the setting can be persisted
claims.text:
🟡 **Medium**

**Avoid committing a photo variant before the setting can be persisted**

The reprocessing helpers have already uploaded and updated `photos.processed_url` before this listing update is attempted. If this update fails, the endpoint returns 500 but leaves the newly generated variant in place while the old `skip_background_removal` value remains. Since consumers now always prefer `processed_url`, users can see a variant that contradicts the persisted setting; concurrent intake processing can create the same mismatch by overwriting this URL after the toggle. Use a persisted processing/version intent and conditionally publish the processed URL only when that intent is still current (or otherwise serialize/reconcile these writes).
